title: Ants meeting a hedge: does foliage stop them?
question: One of these lets an ant push through leaves; the other treats the bush as a wall. Which reads like a real ant in undergrowth? Trunks stay solid in both.
context_md: Same binary, same seed, same hedge -- one env switch is the only difference. Over the longer run of this scene: blocked steps 666 -> 180, tissue among the blockers 94% -> 69%, and leaf disappears from the blocker list entirely (it was 43% of it). What still blocks an ant is wood 82% and rootwood 18%, which is deliberate: an ant walks ON a trunk, not through it. Measured separately on the real world (scene=colony, 4 seeds): living tissue is 18-64% of every blocked step an ant takes in a wood, and 69-96% of THAT is tree trunk, not foliage.
